label: Class 4
name: Class 4
blurb: Bigger numbers, area, symmetry and budgets.

chapters.title: Bigger numbers, factors and Roman numerals
chapters.tagline: Use place value beyond four digits and investigate exact groups.
outcomes: I can build and compare larger numbers.
I can find factors and multiples.
I can read and use Roman numerals.

vocab.meaning: What a digit is worth because of where it sits. The 4 in 40,327 is worth 40,000.
A number that divides another number exactly. 3 is a factor of 12.
A number you reach by skip counting. 12, 16 and 20 are multiples of 4.
A number written with letters such as I, V, X, L and C.

see.title: Five digits, five places
text: In 40,327 the digits sit in ten-thousands, thousands, hundreds, tens and ones.
The 4 is worth 40,000. The 3 is worth 300.
Say it: forty thousand, three hundred twenty-seven.

see.title: Compare from the left
text: Compare the biggest places first.
40,327 and 40,972 start the same. Their hundreds are 3 and 9.
3 hundreds is less than 9 hundreds, so 40,327 is smaller.

c.caption: Hundreds digits 3 and 9: the right side is bigger.

see.title: Factors come in pairs
text: 12 = 3 × 4, so 3 and 4 are factors of 12.
The factors of 12 are 1, 2, 3, 4, 6 and 12.
Every factor pair is one array.

see.title: Multiples are skip counts
text: Count in 4s from 0: 4, 8, 12, 16, 20.
Each number you land on is a multiple of 4.
A multiple of 4 can always be shared into groups of 4.

see.title: Roman numerals
text: I is 1, V is 5, X is 10, L is 50 and C is 100.
A small letter before a big one is taken away. IV is 4 and IX is 9.
XXIX is 20 + 9, which is 29.

try.prompt: Build 40,605: 4 ten thousands, 0 thousands, 6 hundreds, 0 tens and 5 ones.
try.success: A zero holds a place. 40,605 has no thousands and no tens.
try.hint: Leave the Thousands and Tens columns at 0.

try.prompt: Make an array with exactly 18 dots. Its rows and columns are a factor pair of 18.
try.success: Yes. 3 × 6 and 2 × 9 are both factor pairs of 18.
try.hint: Try 3 rows of 6 or 2 rows of 9.

try.prompt: Hop in 6s from 0. Land on the 4th multiple of 6.
try.hint: Press the hop button four times.

try.prompt: Write 14 in Roman numerals. Tap each gap, then a tile.
try.success: X is 10 and IV is 4, so XIV is 14.
try.hint: Start with X for ten. Then IV for four.

chapters.title: Calculate and solve step by step
chapters.tagline: Choose operations, use written methods and check missing information.
outcomes: I can multiply and divide using models.
I can interpret a remainder.
I can solve a linked story or missing digit.

vocab.meaning: The answer when you multiply. The product of 6 and 7 is 42.
The whole-number answer when you divide.
What is left over when a division is not exact.
The number you divide by.

see.title: Split to multiply
text: To find 23 × 4, split 23 into 20 and 3.
Add the two parts: 80 + 12 = 92.

see.title: Equal groups
text: 5 groups of 6 make 30 in all.
That is 5 × 6 = 30.
The same array shows 30 ÷ 6 = 5.

see.title: Divide into equal parts
text: 28 ÷ 4 asks how many 4s fit in 28.
4 × 7 = 28, so the answer is 7.
Multiplying and dividing undo each other.

see.title: Remainders
text: 47 sweets go into bags of 5. That makes 9 full bags with 2 left over.
Check it: 9 × 5 + 2 = 47.
Read the story. It may ask for full bags or for bags needed.

try.prompt: Show 6 groups of 7.
try.hint: Add 6 groups and 7 in each group.

try.prompt: 47 sweets, 6 in a bag. 7 full bags hold 42. Add the left-over sweets to level the balance.
try.hint: How many more than 42 is 47?

chapters.title: Compare and use fractions
chapters.tagline: Keep track of the whole while matching parts and solving changes.
outcomes: I can show equal fractions.
I can find a fraction of an amount.
I can find what is left after fraction changes.

vocab.meaning: The top number. It counts the parts you have.
The bottom number. It tells how many equal parts make the whole.
Different fractions that show the same amount, like 1/2 and 4/8.

see.title: Equal parts of a whole
text: The bottom number says how many equal parts the whole has.
The top number says how many parts are shaded.
Here 3 of 8 equal parts are shaded: 3/8.

see.title: Same amount, different cuts
text: Cut the whole into more parts and the shaded amount stays the same.
Always keep the whole the same size.

see.title: A fraction of an amount
text: To find 3/4 of 20, share 20 into 4 equal groups.
Each group is 5, so 1/4 of 20 is 5.
3 groups of 5 make 15, so 3/4 of 20 is 15.

see.title: What is left?
text: Use 1/3 of 12 sweets. That is 4 sweets, so 8 are left.
The 8 left is 2/3 of the 12.
Follow each change to the new amount, then work out the next step.

try.prompt: Shade the bottom bar so it shows the same amount as one half.
try.hint: Half of 8 parts is 4 parts.

try.prompt: Shade 5/6 of the bar.
try.hint: Shade 5 of the 6 parts.

try.prompt: Share 20 sweets into 4 equal groups. Show 4 groups of 5.
try.hint: You need 4 groups with 5 in each.

chapters.title: Perimeter, area and symmetry
chapters.tagline: Separate the outside boundary from the space inside a shape.
outcomes: I can find a perimeter or missing side.
I can find area using square units.
I can complete a reflection or folded solid.

vocab.meaning: The distance all the way round the outside of a shape.
The number of square units that cover the inside of a shape.
A fold line that makes two halves that match exactly.
A square with sides of 1 unit, used to measure area.

see.title: Perimeter is the way round
text: Walk round the outside edge and add every side.
A 5 by 3 rectangle has 5 + 3 + 5 + 3 = 16 units all round.
Perimeter is measured in cm, m or other lengths.

see.title: Area counts squares
text: Count the squares inside the shape.
This L-shape covers 10 squares, so its area is 10 square units.
Area is measured in square cm or square m.

see.title: Find a missing side
text: Opposite sides of a rectangle are equal.
Add the sides you know. Then take that from the perimeter.
Share what is left between the sides you still need.

see.title: Mirror, mirror
text: A line of symmetry works like a mirror.
Each square has a twin the same distance on the other side.
Reflect a pattern by painting the twins.

try.prompt: Shade a rectangle with area 12 and perimeter 14.
try.hint: Try a rectangle 3 squares by 4 squares.

try.prompt: Shade 4 squares on the left. The mirror shades their twins. Make 8 shaded squares.
try.success: Each square plus its twin makes 8.
try.hint: Tap 4 different squares on the left.

chapters.title: Measure and convert units
chapters.tagline: Read the scale and convert length, mass or capacity before calculating.
outcomes: I can measure from a non-zero mark.
I can combine or share mixed units.
I can use balances and temperature scales.

vocab.meaning: Change a measurement into a different unit, like metres to centimetres.
How heavy something is. We use grams and kilograms.
How much a container holds. We use millilitres and litres.

see.title: Measure from the right mark
text: A ribbon may not start at 0. Look at where it begins.
It starts at 3 and ends at 9. The length is 9 − 3 = 6 cm.
Subtract the start from the end.

see.title: Convert, then combine
text: Add 2 m 60 cm and 1 m 45 cm.
That is 3 m 105 cm, so 4 m 5 cm.

see.title: Read the scale
text: Look at how much each small mark is worth.
Here every tick is 1 degree.
The thermometer reads 23 degrees.

see.title: Balance the crates
text: Three identical crates weigh 1200 g.
Share 1200 g into 3 equal parts.
One crate weighs 400 g.

try.prompt: A ribbon starts at 4 and is 7 cm long. Move the marker to where it ends.
try.hint: Count 7 steps on from 4.

try.prompt: The right pan has 10 blocks of 100 g, which is 1 kg. Add to the left until it is level.
try.hint: How many more than 6 make 10?

chapters.title: Timetables, dates and clock errors
chapters.tagline: Use intervals and distinguish the clock reading from the true time.
outcomes: I can find a missing time interval.
I can use a timetable or calendar.
I can correct a fast or slow clock.

vocab.meaning: The time that passes between a start and an end.
A list that shows when things start, stop or leave.
A clock that shows a later time than the true time.

see.title: How long did it last?
text: A show starts at 8:45 and ends at 10:30.
8:45 to 9:00 is 15 minutes. 9:00 to 10:00 is 1 hour. 10:00 to 10:30 is 30 minutes.
Add them: 1 hour 45 minutes.

see.title: Read a timetable
text: A bus leaves at 9:40 and you are ready at 9:25.
Count on from 9:25 to 9:40.
You wait 15 minutes.

see.title: Use a calendar
text: Count days on a calendar. From 29 March to 8 April: 2 days to 31 March, then 8 more.
That is 10 days.
In March 2026 the 1st is a Sunday, so the 29th is a Sunday too.

see.title: Fast and slow clocks
text: A fast clock shows too much time, so take the gap away.
This clock shows 4:20 and is 15 minutes fast.
The true time is 4:05.

c.caption: Shows 4:20, but it is 15 minutes fast.

try.prompt: This clock shows 4:20 but is 15 minutes fast. Set the true time.
try.hint: Go back 15 minutes from 4:20.

try.prompt: A film starts at 8:45 and lasts 1 hour 45 minutes. Show when it ends.
try.hint: Add the hour first. Then add 45 minutes.

try.prompt: March 2026 starts on a Sunday. Tap the first Friday.
try.success: Sunday is the 1st, so the first Friday is the 6th.
try.hint: Count on from Sunday 1: Mon, Tue, Wed, Thu, Fri.

chapters.title: Bills, budgets and rupees with paise
chapters.tagline: Keep rupees and paise lined up while comparing real shopping choices.
outcomes: I can total a bill and find change.
I can compare equal amounts in packs.
I can choose within a budget.

vocab.meaning: The list of what you bought and the total you owe.
The money you get back when you pay more than the bill.
The most money you plan to spend.
100 paise make 1 rupee.

see.title: Add up the bill
text: Add the prices one at a time.
Rs 50 + Rs 20 + Rs 5 = Rs 75.
Keep rupees under rupees when you write them in a column.

see.title: Find the change
text: Pay Rs 200 for a Rs 130 bill.
Count on: 130 to 150 is 20. 150 to 200 is 50.
The change is Rs 70.

see.title: Compare packs
text: Pack A has 6 pens for Rs 30. That is Rs 5 each.
Pack B has 4 pens for Rs 24. That is Rs 6 each.
Pack A is the better buy.

see.title: Rupees and paise
text: 100 paise make Rs 1.
Rs 2.50 means 2 rupees and 50 paise.
Line up the point before you add.

try.prompt: Pay exactly Rs 75 using exactly 3 coins or notes.
try.hint: Start with the Rs 50 note.

try.prompt: Change for a Rs 130 bill paid with Rs 200 is Rs 70. Make Rs 70 using exactly 2 notes.
try.hint: Try the biggest note first.

chapters.title: Read scaled charts and compare results
chapters.tagline: Use axes, half-symbol keys and totals across displays.
outcomes: I can use a non-unit chart scale.
I can read half a pictograph symbol.
I can compare and update survey data.

vocab.meaning: How much one step or one symbol on a chart stands for.
A chart that uses symbols to show counts.
The note that tells you what each symbol is worth.
Asking a group the same question and recording the answers.

see.title: Read the key first
text: This key says each ● is 2 children.
Count the symbols, then multiply by 2.
Three symbols mean 6 children.

see.title: Half a symbol is half the value
text: If a star is worth 10 stickers, half a star is worth 5.
Add the whole stars and the half star.
Two and a half stars is 25 stickers.

see.title: Compare the bars
text: Find the tallest and shortest bars.
Subtract to find how many more.
Read the scale on the side before you subtract.

see.title: Update the data
text: If 6 samples move from Lyra to Aster, take 6 off Lyra and add 6 to Aster.
The total stays the same.
Check that the two changes match.

try.prompt: Each ● is 2 children. Show 14 children for Mango.
try.hint: Half of 14 is how many symbols?

try.prompt: Aster has 12 and Lyra has 18. Move samples so both have the same.
try.success: Move 3 from Lyra to Aster. 15 and 15.
try.hint: The total is 30. Half of 30 is 15.

chapters.title: Codes, turns and hidden pictures
chapters.tagline: Explain each code, picture or ordering rule before selecting an answer.
outcomes: I can use codes and alphabet order.
I can follow turns and ranking clues.
I can find a hidden figure or picture rule.
I can list possible pairs without missing any.

vocab.meaning: A rule that changes letters or numbers into new ones.
Ordering words by their first letter, then second letter and so on.
One choice from each group, like a shirt and a cap.

see.title: Crack a letter code
text: Look for the rule first. In this code each letter moves 1 step forward.
R becomes S, O becomes P, A becomes B and D becomes E.
ROAD is written SPBE.

see.title: Dictionary order
text: Compare the first letters. If they match, compare the next letters.
INK, KITE, LAMP, PIN, SUN is in dictionary order.
Say the alphabet in your head to check.

see.title: Follow the moves
text: Read each command and move one square.
Walls block the way.
Plan the whole route before you run it.

see.title: List every pair
text: 3 shirts and 2 caps make 3 × 2 = 6 outfits.
List the outfits in order so none are missed or repeated.
An array can help you count them.

try.prompt: Guide the rover to the flag with the compass commands.
try.success: North three times, then east three times.
try.hint: Go up the left side, then along the top.

try.prompt: Put the words in dictionary order. Tap a gap, then a word.
try.success: I, K, S: INK, KITE, SUN.
try.hint: Which first letter comes earliest in the alphabet?

try.prompt: 3 shirts and 2 caps. Build the array of all outfits.
try.hint: Make 3 rows of 2.
